examples.text: Die Arbeitsgemeinschaft, die sich mit der Qualitätssicherung beschäftigt, wird sich jeden Montag treffen.

„Für den gleichen Tatbestand war auch die Einstellung der Schüler zur Unterrichtsmethodik typisch: Sie sprachen sich in großer Mehrheit für eine mehr traditionelle Form des Fachunterrichts aus, in dem der Lehrer als unterrichtende Fachkraft auftritt, und waren überwiegend gegen Arbeitsgemeinschaften und freiere Formen des Unterrichtens.“
„Leo kannte sogar Marie von irgendwelchen Arbeitsgemeinschaften her, wo katholische und evangelische Jugendliche über Demokratie und über konfessionelle Toleranz diskutierten.“

glosses: An interdisciplinary collaboration of researchers working on new research activities that would be difficult to develop under traditional funding mechanisms such as federal agencies.
Any more or less formal team working for a specific purpose.

translations.source_sense_description: Gruppe von Personen, die zur gemeinsamen Arbeit zusammenkommen

glosses: A room, especially one which is not particularly large, used for manufacturing or other light industrial work.

examples.text: A gleam of sun shining through the unsashed window, and chequering the dark workshop with a broad patch of light, fell full upon him, as though attracted by his sunny heart.

glosses: A brief, intensive course of education for a small group, emphasizing interaction and practical problem solving.

examples.text: On any given Friday night at the Claremont Colleges, between 15 and 20 Jewish students gather to sing wordless melodies, dive into textual study of Talmud or James Baldwin, or hold workshops on antisemitism.

glosses: An academic conference.
To help a playwright revise a draft of (a play) by rehearsing it with actors and critiquing the results.
To work on or revise something, especially collaboratively, in a workshop.

examples.text: Some in-class tutorial time was set aside for workshopping the entries.

glosses: To improve through collaboration.

translations.source_sense_description: Gruppe von Personen, die zur gemeinsamen Arbeit zusammenkommen

glosses: A set of draught animals, such as two horses in front of a carriage.

examples.text: It happened almost every day that coaches stuck fast, until a team of cattle could be procured from some neighbouring farm to tug them out of the slough.
The adjacent alleys were choked with tethered wagons, the teams reversed and nuzzling gnawed corn-ears over the tail-boards.

glosses: Any group of people involved in the same activity, especially sports or work.

examples.text: We need more volunteers for the netball team.
The IT manager leads a team of three software developers.

glosses: A group of animals moving together, especially young ducks.

examples.text: she will wonder to have a teeme of ducklings about her
a long team of snowy swans on high

glosses: A royalty or privilege granted by royal charter to a lord of a manor, of having, keeping, and judging in his court, his bondmen, neifes, and villains, and their offspring, or suit, that is, goods and chattels, and appurtenances thereto.

examples.text: TEAM, Theam, Tem, Them. Sax. [from tyman, to propagate, to teem.] In old English law. Literally, an offspring, race or generation. A royalty or privilege granted by royal charter to a lord of a manor, of having, keeping and judging in his court, his bondmen, neifes and villeins, and their offspring or suit. They who had a jurisdiction of this kind, were said to have a court of Theme... constantly used in the old books in connection with toll, in the expression Toll & Team.

glosses: A group of people who favor one side of a binary debate that is divided and lacks a well-established clear consensus.

examples.text: As Jan. 1, 2020, approaches, it turns out there is a Team Zero and a Team 1 – those who believe the new decade will begin after midnight on the upcoming New Year's Eve and those who believe the burgeoning celebrations of a new decade (and all the "last decade" retrospectives) are in fact a year early.

glosses: To form a group, as for sports or work.

examples.text: They teamed to complete the project.

glosses: To go together well; to harmonize.

examples.text: Rich, creamy avocado is cut back by the citrus sharpness of grapefruit in this Israeli-inspired salad. It's brilliant for a brunchy breakfast, and teams well with grilled salmon, tuna, or mackerel for dinner.

glosses: To convey or haul with a team.

examples.text: to team lumber
the farmer has been all winter teaming wood along the river

glosses: To form together into a team.

examples.text: to team oxen

glosses: To give work to a gang under a subcontractor.
Used to propose that another player team up with the speaker.
Misspelling of teem.
